reading.label: Reading Archive
reading.title: I am what I read
reading.summary: A personal archive for books, moods, notes, and the traces reading leaves behind.
reading.description: This is the central reading archive: the place for books, dates, quotes, first impressions, rereads, and the small evidence of how a text stayed with you.
includes: Book notes
Title, author, dates, quotes, reading mood, and quick response.
Reading traces
Questions, obsessions, and small details that keep returning after you finish.
Reading timeline
A chronological view of what you read and what themes occupied you then.
sample: quiet, fragmented, alert to city sounds
Close Reading Lab: opening sentence and movement through London

criticism.label: My fiction
criticism.title: Welcome to my silly world
criticism.summary: Characters, fragments, scenes, and the private logic of unfinished stories.
criticism.description: This is the writing room: playful, strange, unfinished, and full of fragments that may become characters, scenes, or entire worlds.
includes: Characters
Names, voices, contradictions, desires, and private histories.
Fragments
Loose scenes, images, opening lines, endings, and sentences that want a home.
World notes
Rules, places, atmospheres, and recurring objects.
sample: A house that remembers more than its owner does
Tender, suspicious, sometimes too dramatic on purpose
A blue cup that appears in every room

context.label: Reflection
context.title: Don't lie to me
context.summary: Close reading, sharper claims, uncomfortable questions, and honest criticism.
context.description: This is where the archive becomes more exacting. It asks whether an interpretation is honest, whether the evidence holds, and what the text is really doing.
includes: Close reading
Quote, image, syntax, rhythm, context, and claim.
Argument check
What the claim says, what supports it, and where it might be weak.
Theory notes
Terms, methods, and frameworks that clarify the reading.
sample: The room is not only private space; it is a test of who is allowed to think.
Woolf's rooms, Morrison's houses, inherited memory
Needs a clearer distinction between room and house

fiction.label: Extra
fiction.title: And more...
fiction.summary: Loose notes, side quests, experiments, and anything that does not fit neatly elsewhere.
fiction.description: This is the overflow drawer: extra thoughts, small experiments, lists, links, and future sections that are not ready to become their own room yet.
includes: Loose notes
Small thoughts, saved lines, links, and ideas to revisit later.
Experiments
Formats, visual ideas, interactive sketches, and possible future blocks.
Parking lot
Things that may become a full section later.
sample: A small page for favorite sentences
A map of books by emotional weather
Decide whether it belongs on Home or Extra

motifs.label: Motif Atlas
motifs.body: Track images like room, mirror, city, sea, silence, body, and memory across books and drafts.
motifs.title: Motif Atlas
motifs.description: A cross-book map for recurring images. Motifs help you notice what your reading and writing keep returning to.
fields: room, mirror, city, sea, silence, body, garden, illness, memory
Books, passages, authors, essays, and fiction drafts
What changes when the same image appears in another context?

closeReading.label: Close Reading Lab
closeReading.body: Build a small analysis from quote, image, syntax, rhythm, context, and claim.
closeReading.title: Close Reading Lab
closeReading.description: A compact workspace for one passage. It is smaller than an essay but deep enough to become one.
fields: Exact passage, page number, edition, and translation
Diction, image, syntax, rhythm, repetition, silence
What this passage reveals about the whole work
examples: Narrator reliability in a single scene

author.label: Author Dossier
author.body: Collect life timeline, historical pressure, places, works, influence, and reception.
author.title: Author Dossier
author.description: A contextual file for understanding form, not a biography dump. The point is to ask why this writer's work sounds and moves the way it does.
fields: Life events, works, publication dates, historical events
Class, gender, migration, politics, language, education, publishing world
Themes, motifs, formal habits, repeated tensions

seeds.label: Essay Seeds
seeds.body: Keep unfinished questions until they become outlines, comparisons, or essays.
seeds.title: Essay Seeds
seeds.description: A holding place for questions that are not ready to become essays yet. This keeps ideas alive without forcing them to be polished too early.
fields: A sharp problem, not a topic
Books, quotes, motifs, author context, theory terms
seed, collecting quotes, outline, draft, published
examples: Why do some novels break time?
Can a house be a memory container?

comparison.label: Comparison Desk
comparison.body: Place two books, authors, motifs, or periods side by side around one clear question.
comparison.title: Comparison Desk
comparison.description: A structured space for comparative literature. It prevents comparison from becoming two separate summaries.
fields: The one problem both texts help you think about
What changes across form, history, language, or politics

fictionStudio.label: Fiction Studio
fictionStudio.body: Develop characters, scenes, fragments, deleted lines, voice tests, and influences.
fictionStudio.title: Fiction Studio
fictionStudio.description: A creative area for your own writing. It keeps drafts connected to the reading archive without making them feel secondary.
fields: Place, action, sensory detail, conflict, emotional turn
Books, motifs, forms, and sentences that shaped the draft

bookDeepDive.label: Book Deep Dive
bookDeepDive.body: Comprehensive research space for a single book—author, context, themes, and your analysis.
bookDeepDive.title: Book Deep Dive
bookDeepDive.description: A detailed research hub connected to all your reading notes. Organize author biography, historical context, themes, and your close readings in one place.
fields: Basic bibliographic info, your rating, reading dates, and initial mood
Life timeline, influences, recurring concerns, and other works
Historical events, cultural movements, publication story
Main ideas, motifs, recurring images, questions the book raises
Close readings, essay seeds, favorite quotes, your interpretation
examples: Create a deep dive for a favorite novel

interactiveReview.label: Interactive Reviews
interactiveReview.body: Turn your thoughts into interactive Q&A, comparisons, and explorations for readers.
interactiveReview.title: Interactive Reviews
interactiveReview.description: Make your reading reflections engaging and dynamic. Create Q&A formats, side-by-side comparisons, or interactive explorations of the book.
fields: Ask yourself questions and reveal your thoughts progressively
Place two books side-by-side to highlight differences and similarities
Map out key events or character arcs visually
Click through different themes and their manifestations

motifMapper.label: Motif Mapper
motifMapper.body: See connections between recurring images and themes across your entire library.
motifMapper.title: Motif & Theme Mapper
motifMapper.description: Visualize how certain images, themes, or ideas appear across different books and your own writing. Discover your reading and writing patterns.
fields: room, silence, memory, death, garden, mirror, journey, inheritance
See which books share the same themes
Discover what your reading and writing obsess over
Define custom themes to track across your library
examples: Room across Woolf, Morrison, and your novel

reading.label: 阅读档案
reading.title: 我即我所读
reading.summary: 保存书、心情、笔记，以及阅读留下的痕迹。
reading.description: 这里是核心阅读档案：书目、日期、摘录、第一印象、重读，以及一本书如何留在你身上的证据。
includes: 书籍笔记
标题、作者、日期、摘录、阅读心情和快速回应。
阅读痕迹
读完后仍反复出现的问题、迷恋和细节。
sample: 《达洛维夫人》 / 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫 / 1925
安静、碎片化、对城市声音很敏感

criticism.label: 我的小说
criticism.title: 欢迎来到我的荒唐世界
criticism.summary: 人物、片段、场景，以及未完成故事的私人逻辑。
criticism.description: 这里是写作房间：好玩、奇怪、未完成，充满可能变成人物、场景或完整世界的碎片。
includes: 人物
名字、声音、矛盾、欲望和私人历史。
片段
松散场景、意象、开头句、结尾和等待归处的句子。
sample: 一栋比主人记得更多的房子
温柔、多疑，有时故意过分戏剧化

context.label: 思考札记
context.title: 不要对我说谎
context.summary: 细读、更锋利的论点、不舒服的问题和诚实的批评。
context.description: 这里让档案变得更严格：解释是否诚实，证据是否站得住，文本到底在做什么。
includes: 文本细读
引文、意象、句法、节奏、语境和论点。
论点检查
论点说了什么、证据在哪里、薄弱处是什么。
sample: 房间不只是私人空间，也测试谁被允许思考。
伍尔夫的房间、莫里森的房屋、继承的记忆

fiction.label: 其他
fiction.title: 还有更多……
fiction.summary: 松散笔记、支线任务、实验，以及暂时无处安放的东西。
fiction.description: 这里是溢出的抽屉：额外想法、小实验、清单、链接和还没准备好成为独立房间的未来 section。
includes: 松散笔记
小想法、保存的句子、链接和以后再看的东西。
实验
形式、视觉想法、互动草图和未来可能的 block。
sample: 做一个喜欢的句子页面
按情绪天气给书做地图

motifs.label: 母题地图
motifs.body: 追踪房间、镜子、城市、海、沉默、身体和记忆等反复出现的意象。
motifs.title: 母题地图
motifs.description: 跨书追踪反复出现的意象，帮助你看见阅读和写作持续回到哪里。
fields: 房间、镜子、城市、海、沉默、身体、花园、疾病、记忆
书籍、段落、作者、论文和小说草稿
examples: 房间 → 私密 / 性别 / 思想
海 → 迁徙 / 尺度 / 返回

closeReading.label: 文本细读
closeReading.body: 从引文、意象、句法、节奏、语境和论点搭建小型分析。
closeReading.title: 文本细读
closeReading.description: 这是一个处理单个段落的小工作区，比论文更轻，但足够深入。
fields: 准确段落、页码、版本和译本
措辞、意象、句法、节奏、重复和沉默
examples: 一个意象在三段中的变化

author.label: 作者档案
author.body: 收集生命时间线、历史压力、地点、作品、影响和接受史。
author.title: 作者档案
author.description: 这里不是传记堆积，而是用语境理解形式。
fields: 生命事件、作品、出版日期、历史事件
阶级、性别、迁徙、政治、语言、教育和出版环境

seeds.label: 论文种子
seeds.body: 保存尚未完成的问题，直到它们成为提纲、比较或文章。
seeds.title: 论文种子
seeds.description: 这里容纳还没有准备好成为论文的问题，让想法先活着。
fields: 一个尖锐的问题，而不只是一个主题
书籍、引文、母题、作者语境、理论词
examples: 为什么有些小说打碎时间？
沉默什么时候成为叙述？

comparison.label: 比较书桌
comparison.body: 围绕一个清晰问题并置两本书、两位作者、两个母题或两个时期。
comparison.title: 比较书桌
comparison.description: 这里让比较不只是两段摘要，而是真正围绕同一个问题展开。
fields: 书/书、作者/作者、母题/母题、时期/时期
两部文本共同帮助你思考的问题
examples: 伍尔夫 / 莫里森与记忆
卡尔维诺 / 博尔赫斯与想象系统

fictionStudio.label: 小说工作室
fictionStudio.body: 发展人物、场景、片段、删去的句子、声音实验和影响来源。
fictionStudio.title: 小说工作室
fictionStudio.description: 这里保存你自己的创作，同时让草稿和阅读档案保持联系。
fields: 欲望、矛盾、恐惧、声音、历史
地点、行动、感官细节、冲突、情绪转折

bookDeepDive.label: 单书深读
bookDeepDive.body: 为一本书整理作者、语境、主题和你的分析。
bookDeepDive.title: 单书深读
bookDeepDive.description: 把作者、历史语境、主题和细读集中到同一个研究页面。
fields: 书目信息、评分、阅读日期和初始心情
生命时间线、影响、反复关切和其他作品
历史事件、文化运动、出版故事
examples: 为喜欢的小说建立深读页

interactiveReview.label: 互动书评
interactiveReview.body: 把想法变成问答、比较和可探索的阅读笔记。
interactiveReview.title: 互动书评
interactiveReview.description: 用问答、并置比较或主题探索，让书评更有层次。
fields: 并排放置两本书，显示差异与相似
视觉化关键事件或人物弧线

motifMapper.label: 母题关系图
motifMapper.body: 查看意象和主题如何在整个书库中互相连接。
motifMapper.title: 母题与主题图
motifMapper.description: 可视化主题、意象和想法在不同书籍及你自己的写作中如何出现。
fields: 房间、沉默、记忆、死亡、花园、镜子、旅程、继承
查看哪些书共享相同主题
发现你的阅读和写作反复迷恋什么
examples: 房间横跨伍尔夫、莫里森和你的小说
